Vision.title: From "do you have this date?" to an event booking operating system
Vision.lede: The value is not a venue directory. It is connecting real demand to real availability, then running the venue from the same system.
Vision.same_problem: Same problem, a completely different flow
Vision.today_2: Ask about the same date 15 times
Vision.today_4: Spreadsheets, WhatsApp, and a notebook at the venue
Vision.with_4: Calendar, leads, and bookings in one system

Investor.headline: Marketplace captures demand; VenueOS controls supply and operations
Investor.lede: That is why the concept is stronger than a venue directory: transaction, SaaS, and data layers reinforce one another.

Economics.title: Platform economics
Economics.lede: Separate booking volume from real platform revenue and what remains after transaction-level costs.
Economics.health_lede: Measure whether trusted supply actually covers demand, not just how many venues signed up.

Future.flex_title: Flexible dates can dramatically change price and choice
Future.flex_lede: Instead of starting from a venue, show the whole month: which day is cheaper, which has more venues, and which is under heavy demand?
Future.drop_title: DateDrop — an empty date stops being a loss
Future.drop_lede: A venue releases a suddenly-free date at a special price for a limited window, and the customer sees a real opportunity instead of the day passing unbooked.
Future.offers_title: Tell us what you need and let venues compete for it
Future.offers_lede: Instead of a long search, the customer posts a clear brief. Only suitable venues send an offer, and the platform ranks them by price, match, and availability.
Future.offers_needs_value: Outdoor preferred, parking, and a bridal room.

Compare.title: Decide together
Compare.lede: Compare the top 3 venues side by side, then share the choice with the family.
Compare.suggestion_copy: Royal Garden has the highest match, but Luma Hall is cheaper and free on the same day.
